text: Ruta was a retired teacher, and she liked a tidy house. In May her old vacuum finally broke, so she had to buy a new one. She chose a smart robot vacuum and set it up all by herself. Then she spoke to her phone. "Please start the vacuum in the living room, but do not go into the bedroom. I don't want it near my plants." The assistant started the robot and marked the bedroom as a room to skip. "The vacuum is cleaning the living room now," it said. "The bedroom is off limits." Ruta smiled. She may be old, she thought, but she could still learn new tricks. An hour later the floor was clean, and the little robot rolled back to its dock.

Kai was a grandparent who paid the bills at the kitchen table every month. This time the water bill looked high, and he wanted to be careful. He typed fast on his phone: "remind me to pay the electrcity bill on friday and update the due date in my list". The assistant understood anyway. It set a reminder for Friday morning and updated the due date on the bill list. It also told him, "Your water bill is due after a stretch of five days, so you have time." Kai nodded. A clear list always made him feel calm. He put the phone down, finished his toast, and went to make a pot of tea.

The person wants their parcel to come on a different day in April, not the usual one.
Deliver it on Thursday instead
Can you move my parcel to next Tuesday at noon?
Not Monday, I'll be out
Please fix a new delivery time for my package
Could the parcel come on the ninth of April rather than the usual day?
Reschedule my delivery for next Tuesday at noon, please
I won't be home on the usual day, so could you send it on Saturday morning instead?
Change when the courier comes

The person wants a list of gas grills, ranked from best to worst.
Rank the gas grills
Which gas grill is the best?
Show grills, best first
Sort the grills by rating
Put the grills in order, from the top rated to the lowest
What are the top grills people like?
Which ones got five stars?
I'm sorry to bother you, but my old grill just broke and we have a party on Saturday, so could you please order the gas grills in the shop by customer reviews?

Olivia ran a small shop and wanted a quiet weekend in the hills. The night before, she packed her tent and a bowl for camp food, then spoke to her phone. "Hills weather?" The assistant gave the current forecast: clear sky, ten degrees at night, and a light wind on top. Olivia asked, "Packing list?" The assistant read out a short list: tent, warm jacket, water, torch, and food. She noticed she had forgotten the torch, so she put it by the door next to her sleeping bag. "Thanks," she said. With the shop closed on Sunday, nothing could stop the trip. She locked up, loaded the car, and set off before the sun went down.

Person: I turned seventy-two last week and I made a little video. Can you post it?
Assistant: Happy birthday! Where should I post it?
Person: On the family page. The grandchildren will love it.
Assistant: Which video is it? I see three from this week.
Person: The one with my favourite song on the piano.
Assistant: Found it. I posted it on the family page.
Person: Thank you. Can you remind me about the doctor appointment on Friday?
Assistant: Yes, I will remind you on Friday morning.

Most phones and speakers can read you the news. It is for people who want to know what is happening without sitting down with a paper. You can change the topics, such as sports, local news or weather. Many people say things like "Give me the sports headlines," "Skip this story," or "Read me the news every morning at seven." You can also ask for fewer stories or a shorter summary. If you only care about your town, you say "Just local news, please." Some people ask for movie news on Fridays. If you are tired of a topic, say "No more politics," and it will stop showing it.

Sabine had just finished a night shift. Her eyes were heavy and her coffee was weak. At half past six she sat on the bus and picked up her phone. "Read my unread emails," she said. The assistant counted a dozen new messages and read out the names of the senders. One was from her manager about next week's shifts. "Write back and say I can work Thursday," she said. The assistant wrote a short reply and asked her to confirm. Another email came with a long attachment. "Explain what it says," she asked. The assistant gave a two-sentence summary. Sabine pressed send, then closed her eyes until her stop.

Booking a table tells the restaurant when you are coming and how many people there will be. Menus and opening hours help you choose a place. Some restaurants are tight on space at the weekend, so booking early is smart. On a website you click the time you want, or you can ask your phone. People often change the day, the time or the number of guests. They say "Make it for six people," "Move it to half past seven," or "Cancel my table." If the Busy Bee is full on Friday, you might ask, "Is there a table later?" For takeaway, people say "Order the same as last time."

name: plan_weekly_meals
does: Plans dinners for the week and can translate a recipe from another language into plain steps, which helps on a foggy day when nobody wants to go shopping.
inputs: how many people are eating, any foods to avoid, and how old the girl or boy is if the meals go in a lunch box
people say:
- What should we eat this week?
- Plan dinners for Monday to Friday
- I need vegetarian meals for four people
- Something quick for tonight, nothing with nuts
- Give me lunch box ideas for my daughter
- Can you turn this Italian recipe into easy English steps?

A bill shows what you owe and when to pay it. If you pay late, some companies add a fee. Many people set a reminder a few days before the due date. They also change how they pay, by card or by bank transfer. People say "Remind me about the rent on the first," or "How much was last month's water bill?" Some ask to round the amount up so it is easy to budget. They also check shop payments, like asking, "Did my payment for the pillow go through?" If a bill looks too high, they say "Show me the last three months."

Sun cream protects your skin at the beach. The number on the bottle shows how strong it is. A tiny bit is not enough, so people put on a lot and do it again after swimming. You can buy it at a pharmacy. Tides tell you when the sea comes in and goes out. People ask their phone to calculate when the tide is low, or say "What is the water temperature today?" or "Remind me to put on more sun cream in two hours." Before going, they also ask for the sun level and for the best time to swim.

The person wants to brush up on when their yearly car insurance bill is due, and get a reminder.
When is my insurance due?
Remind me about the car insurance
Set a reminder for the yearly bill
Tell me when the insurance has to be paid, please
Remind me a week before it is due, with my favourite song as the sound. Actually, no, a plain beep is fine.
Ping me before the car insurance runs out
Could you check the date for my yearly insurance and set an alert three days before? I keep forgetting.
Remind me on the fifth, sorry, I mean the fifteenth

Person: Please mow the lawn.
Assistant: Which part, the front, the back or both?
Person: Just the back. And cut it shorter than last time.
Assistant: How much shorter? I can cut it half an inch lower.
Person: Half an inch is fine. The grass looks lovely after the rain, but it grows so fast.
Assistant: Done. I will mow the back lawn at the lower setting.
Person: Can you hold the mower until my girl finishes playing outside?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't see where she is, but I can wait until four o'clock if you like.
Person: Four is good.

A smart speaker plays music, answers questions and controls other devices at home. It is linked to your account, so it knows your lists and your voice. People change the volume, pick a different voice, or put speakers into a group so one song plays in every room. They say "Turn it down," "Play this in the kitchen too," or "Pull up my shopping list." A speaker is not dangerous, but it is wise to check who can use it. When a guest is loud and you want calm, you can say "Quiet mode." If you want it to stop listening for a while, you say "Mute the microphone."

The person wants a stronger cup of their favorite coffee.
Stronger, please
Make my coffee stronger
More coffee, less water
Brew it bold this time
It tasted weak yesterday, can you make it stronger?
Make it a medium, no wait, make it strong
Bill likes it black and strong, so brew a big pot like that, and put it on the bill
I'm so sleepy today, could you please brew a very strong cup, because I have a long drive?

Aiko owned a small shop, and on Sunday she liked to look after her lawn. That evening she told the garden app, "Start the sprinkler for twenty minutes." Then she remembered the wine tasting that night, with guests coming to the garden after dinner. "No, wait, make it ten minutes," she said. "I don't want the grass wet when the guests come." The assistant changed the timer to ten minutes and said it would stop the sprinkler at six. The grass felt soft under her feet. At six the water stopped, and the guests sat down with their wine on dry grass.

Person: I just moved here and the wifi is very slow. Can you fix it?
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. Which router do you have?
Person: I'm not sure. It's the white box near the TV. I have an online exam tomorrow.
Assistant: Let's start with a restart. Do you want me to switch the router off and on?
Person: Yes, but not now, I'm on a call. Do it at ten.
Assistant: Ten tonight, understood.
Person: Sorry, ten is too late. Make it nine.
Assistant: Okay, I will switch it off and on at nine.

The person wants to download more bedtime stories for the kids and forward the list to their partner.
Download more stories for the kids
Get me two more stories, ones that are shorter than last night's
Put double the bedtime stories on the tablet
Can you download the story about the sour lemon again?
More bedtime stories, please
Forward the story list to my wife so she can pick too
Half of the new ones should be short, the rest can be long
We ran out of stories, so would you mind saving a few more on the tablet before bed?

Ishaan, a gardener, came in from the garden with muddy boots. His new coffee machine had a frequent problem: it beeped and showed a message in German. "Translate the message on my coffee machine," he said, holding his phone up to the screen. The assistant read the words and told him that the water tank was empty. Ishaan filled the tank and wiped his hands. Then he said, "Make me a coffee before lunch on Sunday, I'll be back from the market." The assistant set the machine to start a cup at eleven on Sunday. The beeping stopped, and the problem was gone.

name: set_light_scene
does: Turns a room's lights to a saved scene, like full brightness or a soft glow, or deletes a scene you do not use any more.
inputs: the room, like the kitchen or the room with the washer, the name of the scene, and whether to use it or delete it
people say:
- Make the living room cosy
- Full brightness in the hall, please
- I'm reading, give me a warm light
- Get rid of my movie night lights
- I can't see a thing by the washer
- Set the kitchen to dinner mode

Sigrid was a student with tired eyes, and she was late for class. On the bus she put in her wireless earbuds and typed fast: "raed my notes alout". The assistant understood and began to read her notes in a calm voice. On the way she walked past a big green bush, and the sun made her phone hard to see. She asked for bigger text, and the letters grew. The assistant said the notes would take about eleven minutes to read, and she asked it to round that to ten for her timetable. It did. Sigrid listened all the way to the school gate and arrived just in time.

The person wants the speaker to flash its light instead of ringing when a timer ends.
Flash the light when the timer is done
Don't ring, just light up
Set a silent timer with a light
Timer for ten minutes, no wait, twenty, and no sound
The ice is in the freezer, so set a timer for four hours and flash at the end
I can't hear anything with my headphones on, so flash instead of beeping
Please flash instead of ringing, I'm in the freezing garage with the door shut and I won't hear it

Ayesha was a student, and her baby brother was asleep in the next room. She was working on homework in the kitchen, with the blender still on the counter from making baby food. The monitor made a small noise, and she typed fast: "close the nusery blinds". The assistant closed the blinds in the baby's room, and the light dimmed. Then she typed, "when is the next feding". The assistant checked the log. The last feeding had been at three, so the next was at six. It offered a reminder, and Ayesha said yes. Then she went back to her books, working quietly.

Jonas was a teenager, and he was texting his friend from the attic, where his band practised. The day was cloudy, and the room was dim. He typed to his phone assistant, "Call Marco." The assistant asked, "Marco Rossi or Marco Lee?" Jonas wrote, "The one who likes to cook." The assistant called Marco Rossi. Nobody picked up, so Jonas said, "Leave a voicemail. Tell him to bring the two hundred flyers." The assistant recorded the message and sent it. Jonas put the phone on the amp and tuned his guitar while he waited for an answer.

Dragan had finished a night shift and was very hungry. He didn't hang around the hospital. On the walk home he took out his phone and typed fast: "is the noodel place on main st open yet". The assistant answered that the Noodle House opened at seven and was open for takeaway. A teacher from his building had told him about the place, and he was glad he was not too late. "Order the usual for pickup," he said. The assistant sent the order and said it would be ready in fifteen minutes. Dragan picked up the warm bag and took it home to eat before sleeping.

Isaac worked in an office, and his mother lived alone across town. At lunch he ate a pancake at his desk and spoke to his phone. "Call Mum." The assistant called, but she did not answer. "Video call," he said. The assistant tried the video call, and this time his mother's face appeared, small on the screen. "Zoom in," he said, and the picture grew bigger. She smiled and told him she had taken her pills. "Pill reminder," Isaac added. The assistant set a daily reminder for eight in the morning. He promised to be back to visit on Sunday and put the phone away.

Person: Please start my book at half past six.
Assistant: Which book? You have two on the go.
Person: The cooking one. I read a chapter daily while dinner cooks.
Assistant: Got it. I will start the cooking book at half past six. Should I begin at chapter nine?
Person: Yes. And can you charge my e-reader?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't charge it. Please plug it in. I can remind you, though.
Person: Fine. Remind me to buy a cucumber, too.
Assistant: I added a cucumber to your shopping list.

The person wants to know if their food delivery is almost here, and if the driver is drawing near.
Where's my food?
How long until the food gets here?
Is the driver close?
Track my order
Tell me when the driver is drawing near
How many more minutes for my pizza?
Would you mind telling me where my driver is? I have a degree class at seven and I need to eat first.
Could you check my order status? My phone battery is low and I won't be able to open the app again.

name: next_bus_times
does: Shows when the next bus or train leaves from a stop and can translate a delay notice from another language into plain words.
inputs: the stop or station, the line if you know it, and how long you can wait, for example if you are thirsty and want to buy a drink first; it needs the internet to get live times
people say:
- When's the next 12 bus?
- Is my train late?
- Do I have time to grab a drink before the bus comes?
- What does this delay sign say?
- What time does the last train leave Central?
- Next tram from the market stop

Person: Can you cut my report to half its length? I only have an hour before bed.
Assistant: Sure. Which report? You have two documents open.
Person: The one for my manager.
Assistant: That one is four pages. I will cut it to two. Is that right?
Person: Yes. Keep my favourite sentence at the end.
Assistant: Done. Do you also want me to break it into shorter paragraphs?
Person: Yes, please. And send it to my manager.
Assistant: I can't send it without you reading it first. Please check it, and then tell me to send it.
Person: Fair enough. I will read it now.

Homework is work from school that you do at home. It helps you practise what you learned. Each assignment has a subject and a due date. When the date is close, many students feel stressed, and some get angry at long tasks. People change the due date, add a subject, or set a study timer. They say "Remind me about maths on Thursday," "What is due tomorrow?" or "Set a study timer for twenty minutes." A student who bites a nail before a test might ask, "Quiz me on spelling." Once a task is done, they say "Close my maths list."

The power went out in Victor's flat, and everything went dark. He was a student, and he had a long essay to finish. He held up his phone and said, "Flashlight on." A white light filled the room. "Power cut?" he asked. The assistant looked at the electricity company's website and said the cut was in his whole street and the power would be back by nine. Victor was patient. The phone was almost empty, so he said, "Battery saver." The assistant turned on the saving mode, and Victor sat by the window and waited for the lights to come back.

Lars drove a delivery van, and next week he was moving house. He had many boxes, a mild cold and a sore back from all the lifting. Between sneezes, he spoke to his phone. "Tell the water company my new address. Don't send letters to the old one any more. I don't want to miss my bills." The assistant opened a form and filled in the new address from his contacts. "Do you want the change to start on the first?" it asked. "Yes," said Lars, and he sneezed again. The assistant sent the form and said the water company would confirm it by email.

A bike route shows the way to ride from one place to another. A phone can plan it, count the distance, and show your speed. People change the length of a ride, avoid hills, or choose quiet roads. They say "Find a flat route," "Make it shorter," or "How far did I go?" On a hot day, they might say "Add a stop for water." At home after the ride, a rider with a smart kitchen can say "Switch on the kettle" so the tea is ready as the door opens.

Mariam, a retired teacher, was about to start fixing the brake on her old bike. The new part cost twelve pounds, and the tool cost eighteen. "Add those up," she said to her speaker. "Thirty pounds," said the assistant. "Is that more or less than my forty?" she asked. "Less. You would have ten pounds left." "And half of that?" "Five pounds." Mariam gave a serious nod, the same nod she used when her students got a sum right. Then she put on her coat and walked to the shop to buy the part.

Clara had just moved to the city and knew nobody. A smooth stone from her old home sat on the shelf in her small flat. One morning she said to her phone, "Excuse me, I moved here last week and I'd like to get fit before my sister visits next month, so could you stream a medium workout of thirty minutes for me, with no jumping, because my neighbours live below?" The assistant started a thirty-minute medium workout with no jumping and added a rest day on Sunday to her plan. Clara thanked it, rolled out her mat, and began her first set of squats.

Chloe, a student, opened her budget app and saw that an update was waiting. Her bike needed repair, and she wanted to know if she could afford it. She typed fast: "how much did i spend on food this monht". The assistant said she had spent ninety pounds on food. It also showed her monthly budget. The number was black, which meant she still had money left. Red would have meant she was over. "Good," Chloe said, and she asked the assistant to save thirty pounds for the repair. It moved the money into a small pot called Bike.

Aroha, a gardener, came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. Her knee had hurt for a week, and she had put off going to the doctor. She said to her phone, "Doctor appointment." The assistant asked, "Make one for this week?" "Yes. Friday." The assistant made the booking at the clinic for Friday at ten and told her it was done. It was a small task, but she was glad to have it finished. "Pill reminder," she added, and the assistant set one for after breakfast. She hoped the pain would go away soon, and she went to wash her hands.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. Voicemail takes a message when nobody answers. You can switch to speakerphone so others in the room can hear. On a call with a teacher or a group, you might mute yourself in a noisy place and unmute when you want to speak. People say "Call Mum," "Put it on speaker," "Mute me," and "Unmute." If the voice is too quiet, they say "Louder, please." They also say "Show me my missed calls" and "Play my voicemail."

The person wants to resume a study timer they paused.
Resume my study timer
Continue the timer
Start again where I stopped
Pick up my ice age revision where I left off
Unpause the study session
I paused for lunch, so please resume the timer, no wait, make it twenty minutes this time
It is rare that I study this late, but could you please resume my timer, because my exam is on Monday?

Alessandro worked in an office on the top floor, and the afternoon sun was hot on his screen. "Close blinds," he said. The assistant lowered them, and the room turned dim and cool. A little later his phone showed a payment notice for the grill he had ordered for the weekend. He read it and smiled. "Blinds half," he said, because he wanted some daylight back. The blinds rose to the middle. It was the last hour of the day. At five he said, "Blinds up," and the assistant opened them all the way before he went home.

The person wants to know if their plane is on time.
Is my flight on time?
Any delay on flight four hundred twelve?
Is the plane late?
What's the status of my flight to Lisbon?
Has the plane left yet?
Check flight number ninety-five for me, please
If the plane is late, I win an extra hour of sleep, so is it?
Could you tell me whether my flight has any delay? I have to decide when to leave for the airport.

Giorgio, a nurse, came home after a night shift wanting nothing but sleep, but his hair needed a cut. He asked his phone, "Book me a haircut for tomorrow, and find a place that is less busy than last time." The assistant said that Pink Scissors had more space on Tuesday at four. "Is it open late?" he asked. "Until eight," said the assistant. A friend had told him the shop was good, and he hoped to win a little peace there. "Book it," he said. The assistant booked the haircut and added it to his calendar. Giorgio lay down and fell asleep at once.

The person wants to know how much electricity the house used today.
How much power did we use today?
Show my electricity use
What's the house using right now?
How much are the solar panels delivering this afternoon?
Tell me, in plain words, how much power we used this week
Show last month, no, I mean this month
How much have I paid for power so far this year? Actually, only this month.
Could you tell me how much electricity we used yesterday? I want to see if the new fridge helps.

Contacts are a list of people you know, with their names, phone numbers, addresses and birthdays. You use them to call or send a message without remembering numbers. People add a new friend, fix a number, or delete an old one. They say "Add Sam, his number is on this card," "Change Ana's address," or "When is Dad's birthday?" A kind note can be added too, like "Has a hamster named Biscuit." When they get a new phone, people say "Push my contacts to the new phone" so nobody is lost.

Sylvie was a cook, and her mornings began with coffee. She had a digital coffee machine in the kitchen, plugged in with a long cable. She planned to sell iced coffee at the weekend market, so she told her speaker, "Make a big jug of iced coffee, the strong kind." Then she changed her mind. "Actually, make it medium strength. My customers don't like it bitter." The assistant changed the setting to medium and started the machine. Soon the kitchen smelled sweet and warm, and Sylvie poured the first cup to taste it.

The person wants to know if there is a water leak in the house.
Is there a leak?
Check for leaks
Why is my water bill so high?
Is water running somewhere?
Look for a leak, I think the pipe under the sink is dripping
Is the basement going to flood?
The water pressure seems too strong in the shower, is something wrong?
I'm so sorry to ask, but I washed my bike tire in the yard and now I can't tell if the tap is still running, so could you check the water flow for a leak?

Bence, a retired teacher, sat in his kitchen in a soft old chair, and the fridge hummed in the corner. "Excuse me, could you please stop reading the sports news and read the local news instead, because I want to know if the road by my house is closed?" he asked. The assistant stopped the sports and read the local headlines. A water pipe on Mill Road was being repaired, and the road would be closed until Thursday. Bence nodded, thanked it, and got up to take the milk out of the fridge for his tea.

name: resume_episode
does: Plays a podcast episode or audiobook from the spot where you left off, at the speed you choose, and checks the show's feed for new episodes.
inputs: the name of the show or book, the artist or author if two have the same name, and the speed; the title is the most important part
people say:
- Carry on with my book
- Where did I stop in the history podcast?
- Play the next chapter, a bit faster
- Any new episodes of the cooking show?
- Put on that podcast I was listening to in the car
- Slow it down, I can't follow
